input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I’m actually in France right now, so I’m abroad. I haven’t really tried making calls or using the internet much, but I mainly noticed the problem when I tried to send a picture message to my daughter. Do you want me to check if I can make a call or use the internet? I’m not sure how to check the mobile data thing.
I just tried again, but it still won’t let me send the picture message. What should I do next?
Looking at the top of my phone, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. Does that mean something’s wrong?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now at the top, it says “No Signal” and something about data being disabled. I still don’t see any bars or 4G/5G. What should I do next?

It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what that means—does that mean my SIM card isn’t working? I also tried to turn on mobile data, but it still says data is disabled. What should I do now?
Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see a few bars at the top, and it says “2G,” but it still says data is disabled. Is that better? What should I do next?

Okay, I turned on mobile data and changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G. Now I see a lot of bars at the top, and it says “5G” with data enabled. Should I try sending the picture message again now?
I just tried to send the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why is this so complicated?

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said. But now it says they’ll reset when I restart the phone. I’m a bit nervous—if I reboot my phone, will I lose my photos or anything important? I really don’t want to lose anything.

My phone restarted and everything looks the same at the top—still says 5G and data is enabled. But I tried sending the picture message again, and it still won’t go through. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really hoping to get this working soon.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I do next? Should we look at the messaging app permissions you mentioned?

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for the phone. It doesn’t have permission for storage or SMS. Should I turn those on? Will that help with sending picture messages?

I turned on both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send the picture message. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really starting to worry this will never work.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you with your MMS issue.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I just tried again, but it still won’t let me send the picture message. What should I do next?

Thank you for trying again. Since enabling roaming didn’t resolve the issue, let’s continue troubleshooting. I’ll guide you through a few checks on your phone to identify the problem.

First, could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- Do you see any signal bars, or does it say “No Signal”?
- Is there an airplane icon (✈️) showing?
- Do you see any indication of mobile data (like 4G, 5G, LTE, or similar)?

This information will help me determine if your phone is connected to the network and if mobile data is active, which are both required for sending MMS.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Looking at the top of my phone, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. Does that mean something’s wrong?

Thank you for checking. The airplane icon means your phone is in Airplane Mode, which disables all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data. That’s why you’re unable to send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once it’s off, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the network. After that, check if you see signal bars and a mobile data indicator (like 4G or 5G) at the top of your screen.

Once you’ve done this, try sending your picture message again and let me know if it works or if you see any new icons or messages.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now at the top, it says “No Signal” and something about data being disabled. I still don’t see any bars or 4G/5G. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you’re seeing “No Signal” and data is disabled, your phone is not currently connected to any cellular network, which is required for sending MMS.

Let’s try the following steps:
1. Make sure your SIM card is properly inserted and active.
2. Check if your phone’s mobile data is enabled.

Could you please:
- Check if your SIM card is recognized by your phone (look for any messages about “No SIM” or “SIM error”).
- Try enabling mobile data in your phone’s settings.

Let me know if you see any messages about your SIM card, or if you’re able to enable mobile data. If you’re unsure how to check these, I can guide you through the steps.
No SIM card detected in the phone.

Mobile Data is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what that means—does that mean my SIM card isn’t working? I also tried to turn on mobile data, but it still says data is disabled. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it means your phone cannot connect to the cellular network, which is why you can’t send MMS or use mobile data.

Let’s try a simple step that often fixes this issue:
- Please power off your phone, remove the SIM card, wait a few seconds, and then reinsert the SIM card securely.
- Power your phone back on and check if the SIM card is now detected (look for signal bars or your carrier’s name at the top of the screen).

After you’ve done this, let me know if your phone now recognizes the SIM card and if you see any signal bars or mobile data indicators. If it still doesn’t work, please let me know.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see a few bars at the top, and it says “2G,” but it still says data is disabled. Is that better? What should I do next?

That’s progress! Your phone now detects the SIM card and is connected to the network (showing signal bars and “2G”). However, “2G” is a very basic network and may not support MMS or reliable mobile data, and data is still disabled.

Let’s do the following next:
1. Enable mobile data on your phone (if you haven’t already).
2. Change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, which are required for MMS and better data connectivity.

Could you try enabling mobile data in your phone’s settings? If you’re not sure how, I can guide you.

After that, please change your network mode to “4G/5G preferred” in your phone’s network settings. If you need help with this step, let me know your phone model and I’ll provide instructions.

Once you’ve done both, let me know if you see “4G” or “5G” at the top of your screen and if you’re able to send your picture message.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned on mobile data and changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G. Now I see a lot of bars at the top, and it says “5G” with data enabled. Should I try sending the picture message again now?

Yes, that’s perfect! Now that you see “5G” and data is enabled, your phone is connected to a network that fully supports MMS and mobile data.

Please try sending your picture message again. Let me know if it goes through successfully or if you encounter any issues.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried to send the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why is this so complicated?

Thank you for your patience—I understand this can be frustrating. Since your phone now has a strong 5G signal and data is enabled, but MMS still isn’t working, the next most common cause is an issue with your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS to work.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to default. Here’s what you need to do:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find the “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network” section.
3. Look for “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
4. Select the option to “Reset to Default” or “Reset Settings.”

After resetting the APN settings, please restart (reboot) your phone.

Once your phone is back on, try sending the picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you need help finding the APN settings on your device.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said. But now it says they’ll reset when I restart the phone. I’m a bit nervous—if I reboot my phone, will I lose my photos or anything important? I really don’t want to lose anything.

Rest assured, restarting (rebooting) your phone will not delete your photos, messages, or any important data. It simply turns your phone off and back on, which is necessary for the new APN settings to take effect.

You can safely restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending your picture message again. If you have any concerns or run into any issues after the restart, let me know right away—I’m here to help!

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...

Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

My phone restarted and everything looks the same at the top—still says 5G and data is enabled. But I tried sending the picture message again, and it still won’t go through. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really hoping to get this working soon.

Thank you for letting me know. Since you have a strong 5G signal, data is enabled, roaming is active, and your APN settings have been reset, there are just a couple more things we can check that sometimes affect MMS:

1. Wi-Fi Calling: If Wi-Fi Calling is enabled, it can sometimes interfere with MMS when abroad.
2. Messaging App Permissions: The messaging app needs permission to access storage and SMS.

Let’s start by checking if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled. Could you please check your phone’s settings and let me know if Wi-Fi Calling is turned on? If it is, please turn it off and try sending the picture message again.

If that doesn’t resolve the issue, we’ll check your messaging app’s permissions next. Let me know what you find!
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I do next? Should we look at the messaging app permissions you mentioned?

Yes, let’s check your messaging app’s permissions next. The app needs permission to access storage (for photos) and SMS (for sending messages).

Please do the following:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Locate your messaging app (it might be called “Messages” or “Messaging”).
4. Tap on it and look for “Permissions.”
5. Make sure both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled.

After confirming or enabling these permissions, try sending your picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you need help finding the permissions settings on your device.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for the phone. It doesn’t have permission for storage or SMS. Should I turn those on? Will that help with sending picture messages?

Yes, please enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for your messaging app. These permissions are required for the app to access your photos (for sending picture messages) and to send/receive SMS/MMS.

Once you’ve enabled both permissions, try sending your picture message again. This should resolve the issue if permissions were the cause.

Let me know if it works or if you encounter any issues!

I turned on both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send the picture message. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really starting to worry this will never work.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. You’ve already tried all the standard troubleshooting steps: enabling roaming, ensuring a strong signal and data connection, resetting APN settings, disabling Wi-Fi Calling, and granting the necessary app permissions.

Since the issue still persists after all these actions, this may require more advanced technical support or a deeper investigation into your account or device configuration.
